phases.name: Scope and identity

steps.action: Confirm document identity: title, release date, version, SHA-256 fingerprint and page count.
Confirm the PDF outline bookmarks match the registered source exactly.
Record the full 15-card-type Introduction list and the separate 16-card-type Table 1/Table 2 list; flag the difference for review.
Obtain SME sign-off on the scope record.

deliverables: Document identity and scope record in the training package
acceptanceCriteria: Fingerprint, page count and outline match the registered source
The Introduction/table card-type mismatch is explicitly recorded

phases.name: Source inventory

steps.action: Classify every section as overview, note, table row or cross-reference.
Anchor each item to a page-local quote, page ID and page text hash.
Prove that all 16 Table 1 rows and all 16 Table 2 rows are covered by at least one inventory item.
List the single ATL105 cross-reference (Element 2, Account Number) and the revision-history notes.

deliverables: Source inventory with full table-row coverage
acceptanceCriteria: 100% of Table 1 and Table 2 rows covered
All quotes resolve on their stated page

phases.name: ATL105 and internal reconciliation

steps.action: Compare the Element 2, Account Number referral with ATL105 2026-3 and 2026-4 using quoted, page-local evidence.
Compare the Table 1 Card Type ID column with ATL105 section 10.1.7.3's printed Card Type IDs.
Check internal consistency: duplicate Card Type IDs, mixed PAN lengths, and the Introduction/table card-type mismatch.
Cross-check Visa Fleet PAN ranges against the independently trained Petroleum 2025-1 Visa Fleet BIN prefixes.
Raise an owned question for every non-aligned or internally inconsistent item and obtain SME dispositions.

deliverables: Reconciliation matrix and internal consistency findings
acceptanceCriteria: Every inventoried rule is reconciled or has a tracked finding

phases.name: Card type catalog extraction

steps.action: Derive every PAN range for all 16 card types directly from the source page text, grouped by declared digit length.
Verify PAN range digit-length matches the declared PAN Length column, except declared-wildcard rows.
Verify every low bound is numerically less than its paired high bound.

Record the single externally evidenced check-digit rule (MasterCard Fleet Mod 10, cited from the Petroleum 2025-1 training lesson) and leave all other card types without an invented check-digit algorithm.

deliverables: Structured card-type catalog with 100 PAN ranges across 16 card types
acceptanceCriteria: Every range is source-derived, not hand-entered
Length and ordering checks pass or are explicitly flagged

phases.name: Entry-mode context matrix

steps.action: Combine each card type with its Table 2 Manual Entry, Encrypted PIN Required and IIN Entered flags.
Mark every combination supported, not-applicable or review-required with evidence.
Confirm Table 1 and Table 2 list the same 16 card types in the same order.

deliverables: Card type x entry-mode context matrix
acceptanceCriteria: Every combination has a disposition and evidence

phases.name: Independent BR derivation

steps.action: Write one atomic BR per card type stating its IIN Length, PAN Length(s) and PAN range(s).
Attach source anchors and the ATL105 Element 2 dependency to every BR.
Exclude Debit and EBT from range-boundary BRs since their declared length is a placeholder, not a fixed structure.

acceptanceCriteria: Every BR is atomic and anchored
Placeholder rows are not asserted as fixed-length rules

phases.name: TS, TC and TD chains

steps.action: Derive low-boundary-valid, high-boundary-valid, below-low-invalid, above-high-invalid and wrong-length-invalid scenarios for every ranged BR.
Create test cases and concrete test data computed arithmetically from the verified range bounds.
Validate canonical BR to TS to TC to TD traceability.

deliverables: Canonical IIN Reference Manual training package
acceptanceCriteria: Every ranged BR has a complete chain
Test data is derived, not invented

phases.name: Lifecycle and specialized flows

steps.action: Model the 2021-2 to 2024-1 Visa Fleet PAN range revision and the 2021-1 to 2021-2 JCB/Discover revisions as lifecycle evidence.
Model the 8-digit BIN transition (April 2022) as a specialized flow affecting Visa, MasterCard and Discover only.
Link every modeled transition to evidence and a test chain.

acceptanceCriteria: Every transition has evidence and a chain

phases.name: Validator and mutation

steps.action: Implement a PAN validator (length and range membership) directly from the derived catalog.
Add mutations for range-boundary violation, wrong length, and (for MasterCard Fleet only) Mod 10 violation.
Prove that the validator rejects every mutation and accepts every valid boundary value.

acceptanceCriteria: Valid boundary data passes and every mutation is caught

phases.name: AI artifact intake

steps.action: Obtain an AI-produced IIN Reference Manual BR/TS/TC/TD package.
Compare it with the independent package for coverage, correctness, traceability and test data.
Triage and track every difference.

acceptanceCriteria: Every difference has a triage decision

steps.action: Execute ready test data on the host or simulator.
Record actual outcomes against independent oracles.
Record SME or TBA approval before promoting the context.

guardrails: IIN Reference Manual 2024-1 supplements ATL105 2026-3 and 2026-4; it does not replace either release.
Fleet card rows in this manual are not treated as authoritative over the Petroleum specification without SME confirmation (IIN-2024-1-Q05).
No check-digit algorithm is invented for a card type unless independently evidenced in this document or a verified cross-document lesson.
Retrieval results are leads, not approved rules.
Executable means ready to run; only actually executed test data counts as executed.
No status is promoted without source evidence and a recorded SME decision.
